ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, C and D are two points on $\odot O$, $\angle CDB=30^\circ$, and BC=4.5, then what is the length of AB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $AC$.\\
Since $AB$ is the diameter of circle $O$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle CAB=\angle CDB=30^\circ$, and $BC=4.5$,\\
it follows that $AB=2BC=\boxed{9}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle, with the center labeled as O; A is on the left side of the circle, B is on the right side of the circle, and line segment AB horizontally passes through the center O, so AB is the diameter. C is on the circumference at the upper right, D is on the circumference below, and the figure connects line segments such as CB, DB, DC, among which BC is a chord of the circle. Reasoning: It is known that ∠CDB=30°, which is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is arc CB. Therefore, the central angle ∠COB subtending the same arc CB is ∠COB=2×30°=60°. Let the radius of the circle be R, then the chord length formula gives BC=2R·sin(∠COB/2)=2R·sin30°=R. It is also known that BC=4.5, so R=4.5. AB is the diameter, AB=2R=9.
